dims: rod in tension: D = sqrt(4P / (pi sigma_t)), rounded up to a preferred size
d2 = 2.0 x d, the pin diameter (outer diameter of eye and fork, d0 = 2d), rounded up to a standard size [Bhandari, Design of Machine Elements, sec 4.12, eq 4.26j]
d3 = 1.5 x d, the pin diameter (pin head and collar diameter, 1.5d), rounded up to a standard size [Bhandari, Design of Machine Elements, sec 4.12, eq 4.26o]
D1 = 1.1 x D, the rod diameter (enlarged rod diameter near the eye and fork, D1 = 1.1D), rounded up to a standard size [Bhandari, Design of Machine Elements, sec 4.12, eq 4.26b]
t = 1.25 x D, the rod diameter (thickness of eye of rod B, b = 1.25D), rounded up to a standard size [Bhandari, Design of Machine Elements, sec 4.12, eq 4.26n]
t1 = 0.75 x D, the rod diameter (thickness of each fork eye, a = 0.75D), rounded up to a standard size [Bhandari, Design of Machine Elements, sec 4.12, eq 4.26m]
t2 = 0.5 x D, the rod diameter (thickness of pin head), rounded up to a whole mm [NPTEL IIT KGP M4L2 fig 4.2.3.1]
collar_t = 0.5 x d, the pin diameter, rounded up to a whole mm; modelling choice, not a book value
taper_d = 0.25 x D, the rod diameter (split pin mean diameter), rounded up to a whole mm [NPTEL IIT KGP M4L2]
gap between eye and fork base
clearance = 0.1 x d, the pin diameter, rounded up to a whole mm; modelling choice, not a book value
notes: Sized for 1.25 x the given load (62,500 N), then checked at 50,000 N. That margin is why the checks sit below their limits.
Pin raised to 45 mm for bending (needs 44.8 mm), the same step Bhandari Ex 4.5 and the NPTEL worked problem take. Set pin_bending.mode to 'check_only' to keep the pin equal to the rod.
